Tyrannical

tih-RAN-ih-kul -- from tyrant / tyranny + -ical. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

To be tyrannical is to be cruel and harsh in the use of power.

The tyrannical warlord taxed the villagers into poverty while living in extravagant luxury himself.

Worked Example

History remembers the emperor as tyrannical: he executed rivals without trial, silenced any criticism, and ruled purely by fear rather than law.

Tyrannical describes the cruel, oppressive USE of power -- not just having power, but abusing it harshly and unfairly over people who have no way to resist.

How Tyrannical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

oppressive

oppressive: exercising harsh, unjust control

despotic

despotic: ruling with total, unchecked power

Antonyms

benevolent

benevolent: kind and well-meaning in the use of power

just

just: fair and reasonable

How Strong Is It? — strict → despotic → tyrannical

strict vs. tyrannical

strict vs. tyrannical: Strict describes firm, demanding rules but not necessarily cruel ones.

despotic vs. tyrannical

despotic vs. tyrannical: Despotic is nearly identical to tyrannical, but often emphasizes total, single-ruler control.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — tyrann-

root — tyrann-: a cruel and unjust ruler (Greek tyrannos)

suffix — -ical

suffix — -ical: having the qualities of; pertaining to

Put it together

Put it together: Tyrannical comes from tyrant/tyranny -- from Greek tyrannos, 'sole ruler' -- plus -ical. Tyrannical describes the cruel, oppressive use of power over people who have no way to resist.
